note: Bergman & Beving reported the SAME Jul-Sep quarter two days before the print with Sweden/Finland (the bulk of Alligo) improving, on a $150k/day 3-analyst name whose only bar was set 8 Oct for analyst-change reasons and whose stock has not firmed on the read-through; CEO bought 8% above spot.

+12% in five sessions on peer read-through into its toughest organic comp of the year, with the margin bar unsourced and the last two sales beats sold (-2.3%, -17.0%); 0.59% flat short gives no squeeze fuel, and this name's own report days run 10-20%.

OEM organic +14% / orders +40% and Fastenal daily sales +15.5% both landed after the (unsourced) Q3 bar and against Bufab's own 5.3% Q2 organic, while the stock gave back the Fastenal-day gain; capped by the missing consensus and Bufab's weaker construction/auto mix.

The SERM-linked extraordinary dividend is near-certain to activate and brokers' amounts still span EUR0.4-1.0bn, but on a 22-analyst major at a record high with the mean target below spot the whole edge is worth a fraction of a point.

Direct peer HMS lost ~11.5% over two sessions on broadening component-cost and tariff commentary while Ependion took only the order read-across (+3.7%); the margin half is unpriced on a $110k/day name whose margin disappointments have cost 13-29%, but it is a proxy against a one-analyst EBITA bar.

The lone 8.0 MEUR EBIT bar needs ~1.7 MEUR of paid non-accrued PE fees against 0.73 in Q2 on the company's own catch-up arithmetic, and the implied Q4 of ~12.3 MEUR invites cuts; held small because misses against this house have not been sold here and the stock is already ~15% lower.

Inside a recommended all-share offer the quarter is noise and only an approvals/timetable line can move a 19% spread; since the offer every operating print has moved the stock under 0.5%, so this is close to an honest zero.

Three separate issuers (Tryg weather DKK 83m vs 160m normalised, Storebrand's low Norwegian retail claims ratio, Protector 58.3% vs 79.3%) point to a benign claims quarter against a company-compiled consensus frozen on 14 Oct that assumes only the same ~3pp FLR improvement; ISR beats here pay about +2% and most of the sector move is already in.

An 18% de-rating driven entirely by two downgrades and a peer ad-hoc, against Hiab's own primary document (order book EUR 589m, +10% YTD, positive book-to-bill everywhere) and two consecutive EPS beats of +23% and +11% that paid +9.2% and +11.2%; the Palfinger warning is a real but proxy offset.

The two peer sets cancel: Atlas Copco/Sandvik/OEM orders point up while the closest business-model comparables Addtech (+2% organic) and AddLife (+4%) point down, and the seasonality edge over a three-broker bar is about 1% of EBITA.

A sourced four-contributor bar of EBITA 59.7m sits BELOW last year's adjusted 62.5m while Q2 adjusted EBITA rose 14%, utilisation has improved for a year and headcount is 5% lower; six insiders including the new CEO and the Norway MD bought into the quarter, AFRY's read is strong, and this name has moved +13.8% / +6.3% / -18.8% on exactly this line.

Inwido, Beijer Ref and Systemair all point to a better Nordic quarter (41% of sales) and Nordea trimmed into the print, but rising European HRC hits a company that itself guided to Q3 margin pressure and 45% of sales sits in the Western Europe the peers do not cover; +8% already into the print.

Biopsafe's first full quarter plus an FX tailwind on an unsourced bar builds to roughly +21-24% adj. EBITA on the issuer's own numbers, but every input is public and the headline growth rate mechanically steps down as XGX anniversaries.

+12.9% in 20 days and +24% in 60 on a dividend authorisation that is now largely in the price, into a quarter that laps its own US price increases, APAC +193% and a 6-7% NOK translation headwind; the possible IEEPA refund is a one-off that gets looked through.

Revenue and EBIT were pre-released on 14 Oct and are worth zero; what is new is quality — the SEK 25.7m defence order is ~15% of the 175m, leaving ex-order growth near +2% — plus an unreported weak Q3 cash line and an autumn supplier-change warning, on a stock up 17.6% and above both analysts' last values.

A new CEO's first report three weeks before his own CMD, with an H2 margin-improvement guide SEB already says is unreachable, and no flagged DCT mega-order in Q3 — the item that rescued both of the last two prints; offset by a 30% de-rating, five cut targets and a 5.4% disclosed short that is fuel.

Three straight EBIT beats and a Q2 margin of 11.0% against a Q3 consensus asking only 9.7%, with ~47.5bn of orders already announced versus a 55.6bn bar that needs only normal base flow; held down by 14-analyst coverage, the 8% BofA-driven rally and Inderes's sourced phasing case for a miss.

PLS took FID on P2000 on 16 Oct, two days AFTER TOMRA compiled its own consensus, firming a 22-sorter Mining award while Recycling order estimates sit flat on Q2 (56 avg, 59 max) — the line that drove +11.9% and -25.6% — with the stock unmoved on the counterparty disclosure; capped because the contract value is unpublished and this name has sold off on five of its last six prints.

The quarter was pre-warned on 2 Oct so the weakness is priced; the only new items are unsized — 'further decisive actions' whose sign is genuinely two-way (cost actions preceded +38.1% in Q3'25, yet Q2'26 fell 10.8%) and an EX60 ramp at a tenth of plan that threatens the cash line. Large move, no usable direction.
